correctness.rationale: For a binary support of size t, the first MMS is h=ceil(t/2). With a uniformly drawn costly pair for the second agent, a deterministic first choice with q costly chores gives payoff b_q+(2-b_q)^+ (t-q)(t-q-1)/(t(t-1)), where b_q=max(1,q/h). This is strictly decreasing up to h; beyond h its successive differences times h are 1-(t-q-1)(3(t-q)-2+2(2h-t))/(t(t-1))>0. It has a unique minimum at h; averaging over seeds yields a fixed input pair, so the lower bound uses only oblivious adversaries. A pair-balanced retained r-set, r=t-h, gives an upper bound for all second supports by binning them in pairs or singletons, and zero-support agents cause no exceptional cost. Consequently the worst pair forces equality of all pair-retention probabilities and the unique minimizing size forces |S|=r. Extra zero-cost chores do not affect the lower-bound pair; the upper policy assigns them to agent one. Maximizing over support sizes uses the increasing even subsequence and the smaller following odd values, giving the frozen R_m. The affine construction has exactly 2(t-1) hyperplanes and the required probability, with rejection sampling costing O(log t) expected fair flips. The printed rank calculation is for even t only; the same proof works verbatim in matrix form for every t≥4: summing the common pair probabilities against a fixed item yields diagonal r/t (since r>1), giving eigenvalues r(t-r)/(t(t-1)) on the orthogonal complement of the all-ones vector and r²/t on its span. Full rank gives the stated support bound also for odd t. Independent exact arithmetic for t≤12 corroborated lower and upper bounds but is not needed beyond the proof.

originality.rationale: Pass is for the full finite-support frontier together with the equality characterization of all optimal policies in the all-positive case and its sparse-sampler consequences. The closest paper has the same lower-bound family and upper pair-block argument, with exact finite hypergeometric terms that nearly give the even-size refinement. It gives the limiting optimum, not the all-sampler equality theorem or the full parity-sensitive fixed-support statement. The affine hyperplanes and the rank method themselves are standard design theory, not asserted as new combinatorics.
residual_risks: The prior lower and upper methods are especially close in the even-inventory case. An unindexed exact refinement or an online allocation application of a weighted design could reduce the distinct contribution.
Rank and affine-block facts by themselves are not originality claims.

value.rationale: The exact finite minimax law resolves the small-inventory cases hidden by the asymptotic 5/4 guarantee.
